main_text.p: quam quod vires habere fit exiftimandum, quales ceruorum cornua, quę millibus remediorum nobilitantur, præcipuè verò aduerfantur venenis, suffituque eorum abiguntur ferpentes. Admultos quoq; vsus celebrantur adeps, medulla & sanguis.
main_text.head: De caprilla, hoedina, hircina.
main_text.p: CApris[?] sacerdotem adeo abstinere voluerunt prisci, ut non modo attingere, sed ne nominare quidem aut appellare liceret, siue quod id animal luxuriosum & olidū abhorrent, siue q; tanquā morbidū timerent. Comitiali enim morbo laborare caprās, nec non febribus graues autores tradūt, ideoq; animam forsan iis quam ouibus ardentiorem, concubitusq; calidiores esse. Flatus ructusq; ciere, choleramq; morbum parere, Hippocr. auctor est, quod tamen de nimis[?] tenellis, nimisq; adultis, & non probè coctis vel præparatis accipiendum esse quaedam existimant. Suauiorem caprinam esse, minusque malam, cum syluæ primum noua frequentiq; fronde germinant, virgultaque turgescunt, experientia docuit. Est in exemplis, athletam quendam Thebanum cunctos alios robore præcelluisse, quod sc.caprilla carne vescereCaroca- prilla cur valentif. fime nu- triat?tur, quam valentissimi esse alimēti, ob firmū, lentumque succum, nec facilē dissipabilem apud Arheneum reperitur.
Sed hoedina inter eximias & præcipuè sa- lubres

page.notes: The first note is printed in the left margin in a smaller italic type. Its reading is doubtful: "fime" and "triat" are uncertain, and "Caroca-" may be a corrupted word. The word "nimis" is partly unclear. The initial C of the paragraph beginning "Apris" is a drop cap, so the first word may be "Caprís" or similar; I have marked it as uncertain. The symbol after "siue" is ambiguous and is transcribed as "q;". The final line is the last printed line of the page and is set indented, but it does not carry a catchword.
